children: A recent interest rate hike and the prospect for more presents a fresh hurdle for a once-popular method of sending cash back to limited partners in private-equity funds, despite continued investor pressure to deliver real returns on long-held commitments.

Overall the volume of dividend recapitalizations financed by banks and private direct lenders this year through July fell around 50% to $19.62 billion from $39.6 billion in the year-ago period, according to data from research providers PitchBook LCD and KBRA, a credit ratings company. The decline followed a rebound that propelled such transactions in 2024 and 2025.

The total value of dividend recaps made by banks through the broadly syndicated loan market in July spiked to $4.8 billion, which PitchBook said resulted mainly from a handful of large transactions, including deals involving Blackstone portfolio company Carrix and Stone Canyon Industries-backed Morton Salt. But anticipation that the rebound augured a more robust fourth quarter was short-lived as the total value of loans made last month fell.

Changing private-equity strategies are driving a broader slump in opportunistic financing deals, with sponsor firms holding off on recapitalizing some well-performing businesses because they are preparing the companies to be sold or taken public, said Sam Shaw, a managing director and head of sponsor coverage at Citizens Bank. The Federal Reserve's recent interest rate move also makes such dividend recap transactions more expensive, diminishing the likelihood of a substantial recovery in the fourth quarter.

Although Shaw said that lender appetite remains solid to support well-performing companies, the likelihood that rates remain higher through 2027 is expected to keep proposed leverage levels for recaps somewhat static and may result in sponsors choosing to use less leverage, to cushion their portfolio companies, he added.

Private-equity fund managers and analysts say their calendars are full of meetings with companies eager to gauge investor interest for coming initial public offerings, which span multiple sectors. Blackstone took sandwich chain Jersey Mike's public in late July. Infrastructure-focused fund manager DigitalBridge Group is looking at an IPO for data-center operator Switch later this year. Olympus Partners-backed Accelevation Holdings recently registered for an IPO that would raise as much as $720 million.
As sponsors prepare to exit portfolio companies, a key focus is reducing debt carried by the businesses, Shaw added. That all but rules out dividend recaps for those companies.

Opportunistic lenders have a wide menu of deals to choose from, with many preferring refinancings and growth deals. Because dividend recaps return capital to equity holders rather than reinvesting in the borrower, some private lenders simply pass on these deals or apply much stricter standards to them.

Craig Snyder, co-head of Opportunistic Credit and co-portfolio manager of special opportunities at Ares Management, said these deals tend to be bull market transactions, picking up when markets feel stable. But the opposite is true when the market is volatile.
"The bar is higher," said Snyder. "For a manager to give capital back to a sponsor, you really want to make sure that the [loan-to-value ratio] is something you can get behind."
